sections.title: Prospectus Summary
text: This summary highlights selected information contained elsewhere in this prospectus. Because it is only a summary, it does not contain all of the information you should consider before making your investment decision. Before investing in our Class A Ordinary Shares, you should carefully read this entire prospectus, including our financial statements and the related notes thereto and the information set forth under “Risk Factors,” “Selected Consolidated Financial Data,” “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” and “Business.”

We are a well-established Digital Out-Of-Home (“DOOH”) media company in Singapore. Founded in February 2005, we pioneered the concept of creating a sizeable network of digital screens at the elevator lobbies of office and commercial buildings in Singapore to sell advertising. Since our founding, we have built a significant and highly visible network of digital screens, supported by a core presence in the elevator lobbies of office and commercial buildings across Singapore. Today, we operate one of the largest DOOH platforms for digital screens deployed at commercial buildings in Singapore, based on the number of commercial building locations within our Digital Network Platform. As of the date of this prospectus, our Digital Network Platform comprises more than 800 digital screens deployed across over 500 diversified commercial building locations in Singapore, including premium office buildings in the Central Business District (“CBD”), coworking spaces, business parks catering to various industries and high-footfall retail destinations. We believe that there is only one other significant media owner operating a comparable DOOH network within commercial buildings in Singapore within this segment. …

The risks described below and elsewhere in the prospectus as referenced above are not the only ones to which we are or may be exposed. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also affect our business. sections.title: Use of Proceeds
text: Based upon an assumed initial public Offering price of US$5.00 per Class A Ordinary Shares (the proposed minimum offering price), we estimate that we will receive net proceeds from this Offering, after deducting the underwriting discounts and the estimated offering expenses payable by us, of approximately US$22 million assuming the Underwriter do not exercise its over-allotment option.

The primary purposes of this offering are to create a public market for our Class A Ordinary Shares for the benefit of all shareholders, retain talented employees by providing them with equity incentives and obtain additional capital.
We intend to use the net proceeds of this Offering as follows, after we complete the remittance process:
• approximately 36% is expected to be used for expansion of screen network in Singapore;
• approximately 28% is expected to be used for software purchase;
• approximately 16% is expected to be used for establishing joint venture, merger and acquisition;
• approximately 10% is expected to be used for strategic reserve for regional development; and
• approximately 10% is expected to be used for working capital.

The foregoing represents our current intentions based upon our present plans and business conditions to use and allocate the net proceeds of this Offering. As of the date of this prospectus, we cannot predict with certainty all of the particular uses for the net proceeds to be received upon the completion of this Offering or the amounts that we will actually spend on the uses set forth above. If an unforeseen event occurs or business conditions change, we may use the proceeds of this Offering differently than as described in this prospectus. As a result, our management will retain broad discretion over the allocation of the net proceeds from this Offering. Each US$1.00 increase (decrease) in the assumed initial public offering price of US$5.00 per Class A Ordinary Shares (which is the midpoint of the range set forth on the cover page of this prospectus) would increase (decrease) the net proceeds to us from this Offering, after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable by us, by approximately US$4,625,000, assuming that the number of Class A Ordinary Shares offered by us, as set forth on the cover page of this prospectus, remains the same.

sections.title: Dilution
text: If you invest in our Class A Ordinary Shares, you will incur immediate dilution since the public offering price per Class A Ordinary Share you will pay in this Offering is more than the net tangible book value per Class A Ordinary Share immediately after this Offering.

The net tangible book value (excluding deferred offering costs) of our Class A Ordinary Shares as of March 31, 2026 was US$90,500, or US$0.009 per Class A Ordinary Share based upon 10,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026. Net tangible book value per share represents the amount of our total tangible assets reduced by the amount of our total liabilities, divided by the total number of Class A Ordinary Shares outstanding. Tangible assets equal our total assets less right of use assets and deferred tax assets.

The dilution in net tangible book value per Class A Ordinary Share to new investors, represents the difference between the amount per Class A Ordinary Share paid by purchasers of Class A Ordinary Shares in this Offering and the pro forma net tangible book value per Class A Ordinary Share immediately after completion of this Offering. After giving effect to the sale of the 5,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares being sold pursuant to the offering price of US$5.00 per Class A Ordinary Share, and after deducting underwriters’ discount, and the non-accountable expense allowance payable by us in the amount of US$250,000 and estimated Offering expenses in the amount of US$1,331,037, our as adjusted net tangible book value (excluding deferred offering costs) would be approximately US$21,884,964 or US$1.09 per share of Class A Ordinary Shares. sections.title: Regulations
text: This section sets forth a summary of the most significant rules and regulations that affect our business in the material jurisdiction.

This section sets forth a summary of the material laws and regulations that affect our Group’s business operations conducted through our Singapore Operating Subsidiaries. Information contained in this section should not be construed as a comprehensive summary nor detailed analysis of the laws and regulations applicable to our Group’s business operations in Singapore. This overview is provided as general information and is neither designed nor intended to be a substitute for professional advice. Prospective investors should consult their own advisers regarding the implications of such laws and regulations.
The Employment Act

The Employment Act 1968 of Singapore (the “Employment Act”) is administered by the Ministry of Manpower of Singapore (the “Ministry of Manpower”) and sets out the basic terms and conditions of employment and the rights and responsibilities of employers as well as employees. It generally extends to all local and foreign employees under a contract of service with an employer, with the exception of certain groups of employees, including seafarers, domestic workers and statutory board employees or civil servants. Part II of the Employment Act applies generally and relates to certain aspects of contracts of services, including termination of employment contracts, notice of such termination and liability on any breach of an employment contract. Part IV of the Employment Act sets out requirements for rest days, hours of work and other conditions of service, and applies only to workmen with salaries not exceeding S$4,500 a month and employees (other than workmen or persons employed in managerial or executive positions) who receive salaries not exceeding S$2,600 a month. …

text: The following table sets forth information concerning our directors and executive officers, including their ages as of the date of this prospectus:

Ms. Chee, 46, a citizen of Singapore, joined the Group 21 years ago in May 2005 and currently serves as the chief executive officer (“CEO”) of FMSG where she oversees all day-to-day aspects of the operations including advertising sales, marketing, business development, partnership, strategic planning and new business initiatives. Ms. Chee originally joined the Group as a manager in the business development division for FMSG and was transferred to the advertising division in 2006 and subsequently rose through the ranks as senior manager advertising sales in 2007, associate director advertising sales in 2008 and associate general manager in 2010. Ms. Chee was appointed as the general manager of FMSG on January 1, 2012 and became managing director on October 8, 2018 and finally as CEO in October 2025. Ms. Chee has almost 25 years of media sales and management experience in the Out-of-Home industry. Prior to joining the Group, Ms. Chee worked for MooveMedia, a ComfortDelgro company, between 2002 and 2005. Ms. Chee obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in Business Administration majoring in Public Relations from the Nottingham Trent University in November 2001.

Mr. Liu, 50, joined the Group 19 years ago in March 2007 and is currently the chief financial officer (“CFO”) of FMSG responsible for all finance, audit and company secretarial matters of the Singapore operations. In 2011, Mr. Liu presided over the finance and audit functions of a listing on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong in July 2011. sections.title: Enforceability of Civil Liabilities
text: We are incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands as an exempted company with limited liability. We are incorporated in the Cayman Islands in order to enjoy the following benefits: (a) political and economic stability; (b) an effective judicial system; (c) a favorable tax system; (d) the absence of exchange control or currency restrictions; and (e) the availability of professional and support services. However, certain disadvantages accompany incorporation in the Cayman Islands. These disadvantages include: (a) the Cayman Islands has a less exhaustive body of securities laws than the United States and these securities laws provide significantly less protection to investors; and (b) Cayman Islands companies may not have standing to sue before the federal courts of the United States.

Our constitutional documents do not contain provisions requiring that disputes, including those arising under the securities laws of the United States, among us, our officers, directors and shareholders, be arbitrated.

Some of our directors and officers reside outside of the United States, and substantially all of our assets are located outside the United States, it may be difficult or impossible for a shareholder to effect service of process within the United States upon us or these persons, or to enforce against us or them judgments obtained in United States courts, including judgments predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the securities laws of the United States or any state in the United States.

We have irrevocably appointed Cogency Global Inc. as our agent to receive service of process in any action against us in any U.S. federal or state court arising out of this Offering or any purchase or sale of securities in connection with this Offering. The address of our agent is 122 East 42nd Street, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10168.

sections.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements
text: Focus Media Network Limited (the “Company”) was incorporated in the Cayman Islands with limited liability under the Companies Act on January 27, 2026. The Company through its subsidiaries (collectively referred to the “Group”) is principally engaged in the operation of a digital out-of-home (“DOOH”) advertising network in Singapore.

In preparation for its initial public offering in the United States, the Group underwent a corporate reorganization (the “Reorganization”) to establish the Company as the ultimate offshore holding entity. On March 10, 2026, the Company completed a non-cash share swap whereby Excellent Investment Services Limited (“Excellent”), the holding company that owns 100% interest of Focus Media Singapore Pte Limited, transferred its 100% interest in the Company to Comeback Investment Assets Limited (“Comeback”), and Ms. Hui Ling Audrey Chee (“Ms. Chee”), the ultimate controlling shareholder, concurrently transferred her 100% interest in Excellent to the Company. Following this step, the Company became the ultimate holding company of the Group, effectively controlled by Ms. Chee through Comeback.

At the time of the Reorganization, the Company was a shell company with no operations. Therefore, the Reorganization has been accounted for as a Reverse Recapitalization. Under this method of accounting, the operating company is treated as the accounting acquirer and the Company is treated as the accounting acquiree.

Accordingly, the consolidated financial statements represent the continuation of the financial statements of the operating company. The share capital has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the legal capital of the Company, and all share and per-share data have been retroactively restated to reflect the impact of the Reorganization and the 1-to-10,000 share subdivision as if they had occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented.

summary: We are a holding company with no material operations of our own, and we depend on dividends and other distributions from our Singapore Operating Subsidiaries to fund our operations and any dividends we may declare. This structure could adversely affect our ability to meet our cash requirements and may expose us to additional risks.
If we fail to attract and retain advertisers, our revenue, profitability and growth prospects could be materially and adversely affected.
If we fail to maintain our relationships with our venue partners or secure new partnerships, our network coverage, advertiser demand and overall financial performance could be adversely affected.

Social, economic, political and legal developments or instability, as well as any changes in government policies, in Singapore, could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and business prospects.
Our business is susceptible to cyclical advertising demand and economic fluctuations in Singapore, which may significantly reduce client spending and adversely impact our financial performance.
Our business is subject to seasonal fluctuations in advertising demand, which may create volatility in our financial performance and affect investor perception of our stability.
Our business depends on the continued leadership of our senior management team, and our ability to retain and attract qualified personnel is critical to our success and future growth.
Operational limitations in advertising capacity may restrict revenue growth and client satisfaction.
Any deterioration in market conditions within advertising and media industry in Singapore may affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and future prospects.

We face intense competition from a broad range of out-of-home and non-out-of-home media companies, which pressures our pricing, challenges our market position, and may reduce our profitability and growth potential.

Changes to existing laws, regulations, and government policies, including those governing advertising, media, data privacy, and programmatic advertising could require us to incur significant additional costs or restrict our operations.
Our business performance depends on maintaining a strong reputation among advertisers, agencies, and venue partners, and any damage to our reputation could negatively affect our financial results.
Our past growth rate, revenue and net profit margin may not be indicative of our future growth rate, revenue and net profit margin.
We may implement business strategies and future plans that may not be successful.
Our current insurance coverage may not sufficiently protect us against all the risks we are exposed to and the insurance premium may increase.
The nature of our business exposes us to intellectual property infringement claims and other legal proceedings.
We may be unable to adequately protect our intellectual property rights, and certain brand identifiers we use may be subject to challenge by third parties.
We are subject to credit and payment collection risks associated with our advertising clients, which could adversely affect our cash flow, working capital, and profitability.

You may experience difficulties in effecting service of process, enforcing foreign judgments or bringing actions in Singapore against us or our management named in this prospectus based on foreign laws.
The ability of our subsidiaries in Singapore to distribute dividends to us may be subject to restrictions under applicable laws.

Any adverse material changes to the Singapore market (whether localized or resulting from economic or other conditions) such as the occurrence of an economic recession, pandemic or widespread outbreak of an infectious disease, could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Our Class A Ordinary Shares may face potential delisting if we fail to meet or maintain the Nasdaq listing requirements, which could adversely affect their liquidity, marketability, and overall investor confidence.

Recent amendments to Nasdaq listing standards and Nasdaq’s expanded discretionary authority to deny initial listings may make it more difficult for us to qualify for or maintain a listing on Nasdaq, which could adversely affect the liquidity and market price of our Class A Ordinary Shares.

We are a “foreign private issuer,” and our disclosure obligations differ from those of U.S. domestic reporting companies. As a result, we may not provide you the same information as U.S. domestic reporting companies or we may provide information at different times, which may make it more difficult for you to evaluate our performance and prospects.

If our Class A Ordinary Shares are listed on Nasdaq, there remains a risk that their price could decline, potentially leading to delisting. In such a scenario, broker-dealers might be discouraged from facilitating transactions in our shares, as they could be classified as penny stocks and become subject to the associated rules.
The trading price of our Class A Ordinary Shares may be volatile, which could result in substantial losses to investors.

FMSN Cayman is incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands. Some of our directors and officers reside outside the United States and they do not have significant assets in the United States. As a result, investors may have difficulty enforcing judgments against us, our directors and management.
Our Class C Ordinary Shares could be issued by our Board of Directors in a manner that dilutes the voting power or economic rights of holders of our Class A Ordinary Share.

You may face difficulties in protecting your interests, and your ability to protect your rights through U.S. courts may be limited, because we are incorporated under Cayman Islands law and the laws of the Cayman Islands relating to the protection of the interest of minority shareholders are different from those in the United States.

Our status as a foreign private issuer under Nasdaq rules, will allow us to adopt certain home country practices in relation to corporate governance matters which may differ significantly from Nasdaq corporate governance listing standards applicable to a U.S. domestic Nasdaq listed company.
Our status as an “emerging growth company” under the JOBS Act may make it more difficult to raise capital as and when we need it.
We may allocate the net proceeds from this Offering in ways that differ from the estimates discussed in the section titled “Use of Proceeds” and with which you may not agree.
Our compensation of directors and executive officers may not be publicly available.

We may be classified as a passive foreign investment company, or PFIC, for U.S. federal income tax purposes for the current taxable year, which could result in adverse U.S. federal income tax consequences for U.S. Holders of our Class A Ordinary Shares.

Our multiple-class share structure may render our Class A Ordinary Shares ineligible for inclusion in certain stock market indices, and thus adversely affect the trading price and liquidity of our Class A Ordinary Shares.

Our multiple-class share structure will limit your ability to influence corporate matters and could discourage others from pursuing any change of control transactions that holders of our Class A Ordinary Shares may view as beneficial.

notes.title: COMMITMENTS AND CONTINGENCIES
text: As of March 31, 2025 and 2026, the Group had neither significant financial nor capital commitment.

In the ordinary course of business, the Group may be subject to legal proceedings regarding contractual and employment relationships and a variety of other matters. The Group records contingent liabilities resulting from such claims, when a loss is assessed to be probable and the amount of the loss is reasonably estimable. In the opinion of management, there was no material on-going or threatened claim or litigation as of March 31,2026, and through the issuance date of these consolidated financial statements.

notes.title: CONCENTRATIONS AND RISK
text: Fluctuations in market interest rates may negatively affect the Company’s financial condition and results of operations. The Company is exposed to floating interest rate risk on cash deposit, and the risk due to changes in interest rates is not material. The Company has not used any derivative financial instruments to manage the interest risk exposure.

Liquidity risk is the risk that we will encounter difficulty in meeting the obligations associated with its financial liabilities that are settled by delivering cash or another financial asset. Our approach to managing liquidity is to ensure, as far as possible, that it will always have sufficient liquidity to meet its liabilities when due, under both normal and stressed conditions, without incurring unacceptable losses or risking damage to our reputation.

revenue.heading: Revenues
revenue.text:
We derive revenues mainly from advertising and media services through our extensive DOOH network. The table below sets forth the breakdown of our revenues for the periods indicated:

Our revenue increased from approximately SGD2.3 million for the year ended March 31, 2025 to approximately SGD4.6 million (US$3.6 million) for the year ended March 31, 2026, as we recorded increase in revenues generated from our expanding business as below.

Advertising and media services — over time

The Company provides advertising and media services and recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606. Revenue is recognized over time as performance obligations are satisfied, as the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits provided by the Company. The Group typically measures progress using the output method based on time elapsed or proof of play. Customer contracts generally have fixed prices with no variable consideration. Payment terms typically range from payments received in advance of service commencement to 28 days credit terms. Accordingly, the Company records contract liabilities when payments are received or due before services are rendered, subsequently recognizing revenue as the performance obligations are met. The Company assesses collectability at contract inception and recognizes revenue only when collectability is probable.

ocf.heading: Operating activities
ocf.text:
Net cash provided by operating activities was SGD0.9 million (US$0.7 million) for the year ended March 31, 2026, which was primarily due to: (a) net profit of SGD2.9 million (US$2.3 million) as mainly adjusted for (i) deferred tax expense of SGD0.7 million (US$0.6 million) and (ii) amortization of operating lease right-of-use asset of SGD0.7 million (US$0.6 million); and (b) changes in operating assets and liabilities due to the growth of business, which primarily consisted of (i) an decrease of SGD1.2 million (US$1.0 million) in accounts receivable, net and (ii) an decrease of SGD0.6 million (US$0.5 million) in operating lease liabilities.

Net cash used in operating activities was SGD0.1 million for the year ended March 31, 2025, which was primarily due to: (a) net loss of SGD0.2 million as mainly adjusted for amortization of operating lease right-of-use asset of SGD0.3 million; and (b) changes in operating assets and liabilities due to the growth of business, which primarily consisted of (i) a decrease of SGD0.5 million in operating lease liabilities and (ii) an increase of SGD0.3 million in accrued expenses and other current liabilities.

capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text: Our capital expenditures are primarily related to purchase of property and equipment. We incurred capital expenditures of nil and SGD0.03 million (US$0.02 million) for the years ended March 31, 2025 and 2026, respectively. We expect that our capital expenditures will increase in the foreseeable future as we expand our business, and that our level of capital expenditures will be significantly affected by user demand for our services. To the extent cash flows from our business activities are insufficient to fund future capital requirements, we may need to seek equity or debt financing. We will continue to incur capital expenditures to support the expected growth of our business.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text: Cost of revenues primarily consists of revenue-sharing payments to landholders, license and lease costs and sales commissions. The Group recognizes these costs as incurred, consistent with the timing of the related revenue recognition.

gp.heading: Gross profit
gp.text: Our gross profit equals to our revenue less our cost of revenue. Our gross profit is primarily affected by our ability to generate revenue and the fluctuation of our cost. Our gross profit increased by approximately SGD2.5 million or 345.4% from approximately SGD0.7 million for the year ended March 31, 2025 to approximately SGD3.1 million (US$2.5 million) for the year ended March 31, 2026, mainly attributable to the enhanced monetization of our existing media network and the resulting operating leverage. As our service revenue grew, the fixed costs associated with our operating lease right-of-use assets and infrastructure remained relatively stable, allowing a greater portion of our incremental revenue to flow through to gross profit. Gross margin as a percent of overall revenue for the years ended March 31, 2025 and 2026 was approximately 31.3% and 68.2%, respectively. The significant margin expansion was primarily driven by the operating leverage described above: as revenue grew, our fixed licence costs to venue partners remained stable, allowing a greater portion of incremental revenue to flow through to gross profit. As pDOOH revenue continues to increase as a percentage of total revenue, we anticipate this trend will continue to positively impact our overall gross margin and results of operations.

ga.heading: General and administrative expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses primarily consisted of advisory fees, salary and compensation expenses relating to our accounting, human resources and executive office personnel, and included rental expenses, depreciation and amortization expenses, office overhead, professional service fees and travel and transportation costs.

nonop.heading: Total other income, net
nonop.text: Our total other income decreased by 1.9% from SGD0.2 million for the year ended March 31, 2025 to SGD0.2 million (US$0.2 million) for the year ended March 31, 2026, primarily due to the increase in government grants and increase in financial expenses resulting from foreign exchange fluctuations.
